The front wrapper, of yellow paper, carries the title within an ornamental border: «Trattati d’aritmetica», treatises of arithmetic, published by Baldassarre Boncompagni, with his academies; «I. Algoritmi de numero Indorum», the first treatise of the series; Rome, the Tipografia delle scienze fisiche e matematiche, Via Lata 211, 1857. The lines of the academies (L05-L10) are set in small capitals. Short rules stand below L04, between L10 and L11 and below L12.
The wrapper is torn at the lower right corner; the print of its back (frame 004) and of the stamp on it shows through.
Nothing is printed on the back of the wrapper; the title of the front (frame 003) and the inscription show through in mirror image.
Blank. Faint offset of lines of type and of the stamp of the next page (frame 006) show on the leaf; a stain at the upper right.
Nothing is printed on the page.
The page number «( 1 )» stands at the head of the page, centred, and the signature «1» of the printed sheet at the foot, centred.

L01-L04: the heading of the treatise, centred: its number in the editor's series, «I.», and its title, «ALGORITMI DE NUMERO INDORUM.», in bold capitals; then, in the smaller type of the notes, the manuscript from which the text is printed: Cambridge University Library, the manuscript marked «Ii. 6. 5», leaves 102 recto to 109 verso. «Ii» is printed in italics, and so are «recto» and «verso».

L05: «DIXIT» opens the text with a large initial D, two lines high, followed by «IXIT» in capitals. The printed note in the right margin beside the line, «car. 102 recto.», gives the leaf of the manuscript at which the text begins; transcribed as a margin note.
The numeral «.ix.» (L10, L16, L20, L25) is printed in small capitals between two points, as the Latin text writes numerals.

L25: the four points after «he» mark the place of the figures of the nine letters, which the edition does not print; the editor's footnote (1) says that the gap is in the manuscript too, at fol. 102 recto, line 18. The footnote counts the lines of the page from the heading «I.»: line 25 is L25 of this transcription.

The lines of the text are printed in the spelling of the manuscript: u for v («uidissem», «uoluerit»), e for ae and oe («que», «preter», «quinte»), «yndos» and «indi», and words divided at the ends of the lines with a hyphen. Transcribed as printed.
The subtitle (L03-L04), the folio in the margin and the footnote are set in a smaller type, darker than the type of the text.

Spaces at punctuation (rule of tools/punct.py: after a mark, a space where the gap is at least 12 px or two thirds of the median word space of the line; before a mark, where it is at least 10 px): without a space after the mark, L22 «exposui,hoc» (9 px, the median word space of the line 16 px) and L24 «inueniri.Leuiterque» (8 px, median 13 px). L22: a speck at mid-height between «ego» and «exposui»; not transcribed.
The page number «( 2 )» stands at the head of the page, centred. The page has no signature.

L03: the four points after «diuersitas» mark the place of the figures that show the differences between the forms of the letters, which the edition does not print; the editor's footnote (1) says that the gap is in the manuscript too, at fol. 102 recto, line 22.
L13: «indiget indiget (sic)»: the edition prints the word twice and marks the repetition with «(sic)» in italics, as the manuscript has it.

L17: the vertical bar between «enim» and «possunt» marks the beginning of fol. 102 verso of the manuscript, which the note in the left margin, «car. 102 verso.», names (on the left-hand pages the folio notes stand in the left margin); transcribed as a margin note.
L23: the text spells the name «algorizmi» here, where p. 1 has «algoritmi» (frame 007, L05, L16).

Spaces at punctuation: L16, L17 and L23 are set tightly, with word spaces of 13 to 19 px. After «tria,» (L16), «diximus,», «dicam,» and «re.» (L17) and «Inueni,» (L23) the gap before the next word is 4 to 8 px, the spacing of the punctuation itself, and no space is transcribed; before the colon of L16 the gap is 6 px. Elsewhere the page sets a space before «;» (L06), «:» (L13) and «,» (L30), as transcribed.
The page number «( 3 )» stands at the head of the page, centred. The page has no footnotes and no signature.

Numerals are printed in small capitals between points: «.cc.», «.ccc.», «.dcccc.» (L02-L03, L11), «.ii.» and «.iii.» milia (L04-L05); L13: «.ix. m.», nine thousand, with «m.» in small capitals after the point of «.ix.», and «.x̄.», ten thousand, an x in small capitals with a bar over it.
L16: «superiora (sic)»: the edition marks the form of the manuscript with «(sic)» in italics.
L17: the t of the first word, «et», shows its stem and foot but not its cross stroke and its pointed top, so that it looks like an l; transcribed «et».
L25: «.o. litere», the letter o between points, in roman type.

Spaces at punctuation: L28, «differentia,esset»: the gap after the comma is 7 px, where the word spaces of the line are 15 to 21 px, and no space is transcribed. L01: the two groups of four points, after «hec» and after «.xx», mark the places of the figures of ten and twenty, which the edition does not print; the footnote says that both gaps are in the manuscript too, at fol. 102 verso, line 33. «.xx» has no closing point before the second gap; «(1).Et» is printed without a space after the point (a gap of 6 px, where the word spaces of the line are 14 to 26 px). L06, L07: the numerals of the fourth place, the thousands, are printed with a bar over the small capitals: «.ī.», 1000, and «.īī.», 2000, the bar running over both letters. L17: «.īx̄.», 9000, with a bar over «.ix» that begins above the first point. L20: «ix.» is printed without the opening point.

L12-L19: the figures of the hundreds and thousands are printed with old-style arabic numerals: «.100.» (L12), «.300.» (L13, L15), «.1000» (L18) and «2000» (L19). L13: the figure of two hundred, «figura ducentorum … sicut figura duorum posita … in tercia differentia», is printed «.300.», the figure that L14-L15 give for three hundred; see the critical note. L15: «.300,» has no closing point. L18: «.1000:» has no closing point. L19: «ita. 2000.»: the point stands after «ita», and a word space before «2000».

L29: «.ii.», in small capitals like the roman numerals of the line, for the number eleven written with figures; the old-style figure 1 of «.1000» (L18) has a flag at its top left, and the two letters of «.ii.» the serifs of the small capital I of «.xi».

The tails are much lighter than the print (their darkest pixel 87 to 143, where the tail of a printed semicolon, as in «prima;» of L10, has its darkest pixel at 20 to 66) and thinner. The semicolons of L07, L10 and L12 are printed.

L08-L09, L20-L21: the text writes «millia» beside «milia» (L08 «.x. millia milia milium», L09 «.c. millia milia milium», L20 «mille millium», L21 «centum millia milia milia milium»); transcribed as printed.

L17: the four points of the gap after «eiusdem», where the figure of the example of L18-L28 stands in the manuscript, are spaced apart, «. . . .»; the editor's footnote (1) says that the gap is in the manuscript too, at fol. 104 recto, lines 8-9.

L18-L28: the number of the example is read out place by place: «mille mille mille millium quinque uicibus», a thousand taken five times, 10^15; «centum millia milia milia milium quatuor uicibus», 100 × 1000^4; «octoginta milia milia milia milium quatuor uicibus», 80 × 1000^4; «septingenta milia milia milium[milium] tribus uicibus», 700 × 1000^3; «tria milia milia milium tribus uicibus», 3 × 1000^3; «quinquaginta unum milia milium duabus uicibus», 51 × 1000^2; and «quadringenta milia et nonaginta duo milia et octingenta sexaginta tres», 492,863: in all 1,180,703,051,492,863. Each count, «quatuor», «tribus», «duabus uicibus», agrees with the number of the words for thousand that precede it, the bracketed «[milium]» set aside, except the first: «quinque uicibus» follows four words, «mille mille / mille millium» (L19-L20); see the critical note.

L25: «milium[milium]»: the repeated word stands between square brackets, which are printed in the ink of the text (their darkest pixels 13 to 25, the colour of the letters), in a heavy slanting form; the opening bracket touches the first «milium». Transcribed as printed.

The example (from p. 14, frame 020, L29-L33): 46468 divided by 324. L01-L11: the figures of 46468 written from the right, the divisor 324 under its three highest places, three under four; the figures of the divisor are not printed (L11 «et hec figura earum.»). L12-L21: the quotient figure one, above the first place of the divisor; one by three, four less three leaves one; one by two, six less two leaves four; one by four, four less four leaves nothing, and a circle is written.
